Scope: collector and local roads, potable water, sewerage, storm drainage, irrigation, medium-voltage, street lighting and telecom networks, a sewage pump station and storm drainage ponds for Block J. Contract value 117.4M SAR excluding VAT, 24 months.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted effort (65,419 units in report 98, the same budget as report 97's 523,360 man-hours). At the 24-Nov-2026 data date the project is 81.2% complete against 90.4% planned, behind by 9.3% (SPI 0.90). Since report 97 it gained 1.07% against 0.97% planned, the first week above plan since mid-September, so the gap narrowed slightly from 9.4%; finishing on the contract date would need 3.14% a week.

The forecast finish slipped another week, to more than eight and a half months late. The P6 update of 24-Nov-2026 finishes the project on 02-Oct-2027, 264 days after the contract date of 11-Jan-2027, with −215.5 days of float; that is 7 days later than the 17-Nov-2026 update, and the weekly report gives the same date. With 93.4% of the contract time used, 18.8% of the physical work remains: finishing on time would need 3.14% a week for the 6 weeks left, against 1.07% achieved this week. The chart data's new forecast curve, which reaches 100% by 12-Jan-2027, is not supported by the schedule.

The P6 update moved almost every milestone a week later. Between the 17-Nov and 24-Nov-2026 updates, project completion and most network milestones moved 7 days later, so the critical path gained nothing this week. The storm drainage ponds are the exception: they moved from 29-May-2027 to 23-Dec-2026 (157 days earlier, −3 days of float) with no explanation in the files. The weekly report again matches P6 for completion (02-Oct-2027) and storm drainage, but now gives later dates for road works (27-Sep against 16-Sep-2027) and mechanical works (27-Jul against 08-Jul-2027). The Employer's NOC for the medium-voltage network is now scheduled for 09-Jan-2027, with −61 days of float.

Data notes

Built from the W09 upload (report 98, the P6 update and a separate Procurement file); the previous week's folder (report 97) was used for this-week changes.

  • The milestone sheet states the contract week ("Current Contract Weeks: 97 of 104"), which matches 681 days from handover on 12-Jan-2025 to the 24-Nov-2026 data date, so this is week 97.
  • The effort unit changed back: the cover and Progress sheet give a budget of 65,419 labelled man-hours (report 96's man-day budget), while report 97 gave 523,360 man-hours and the chart sheet still uses 523,354. The Progress sheet's "last week" columns (52,570 earned) do not match report 97 (419,264 man-hours, or 52,408 at 8 hours a day).
  • This week's gain differs by source: 1.07% from the cover's cumulative values (80.11% to 81.18%), 1.03% in the chart sheet (5,370 man-hours) and 0.82% in the Progress sheet's weekly column (537 of 65,419). Planned to date is 90.44% on the cover and 90.60% in the chart sheet.
  • Street lighting is now 28.0% earned against 17.2% in report 97, although the weekly column earns it only 45 units (1.8%). Potable water earns 71 units with no new pipe length, and telecom is reported in progress with no change in quantity or earned effort.
  • The chart sheet's forecast was replaced: it now climbs 2.4% to 3.1% a week to reach 100% on 12-Jan-2027, against 1.03% achieved this week, while the P6 update and the cover forecast 02-Oct-2027. Report 97's forecast reached 100% in September 2027.
  • The Conclusion sheet changed several totals: roads 55,631 to 53,782 t, storm drainage 24,720 to 24,748 LM, sewerage 12,806 to 12,936 LM, potable water 14,405 to 14,048 LM and irrigation 14,494 to 14,523 LM. It lists 47 fire hydrants against 55 in the Major Quantities sheet.
  • The procurement log was rebuilt without order or delivery dates, and several items jumped to 100% in one week (curbstone 0 to 42,552 pieces, panel boards 0 to 6, MV cable 68% to 100%, subgrade 50% to 100%, base course 44% to 100%, interlock 27% to 100%). The LED luminaire quantity changed from 355 to 358 and the telecom duct quantities from 17,620 m each to 14,500 and 13,800 m for two colours.
  • The Major Quantities sheet was recalculated and many installed quantities fell from report 97: capping 45,929 to 39,712 m³, base course 22,365 to 17,550 m³, street-lighting cable 10,217 to 6,294 m and catch basins 461 to 353; storm main lines that were all 100% are now 96% to 97%. Its planned-to-date column also changed (base course 38,412 to 17,550 m³). All 18,200 m of kerb are still shown installed.
  • Quality score: 0.69 on the cover and in the inspection log for 24-Nov-2026, but the Quality sheet header shows 0.92 and its own total is 71 of 116 (61%). FIRs pending are 66, while the ageing column still shows 104 in the 0 to 10 day band.
  • Manpower on the cover is labelled the wrong way round (manual 9 planned / 14 actual, non-manual 143 / 209). The trade table plans 143 manual workers, the Manpower sheet 143.2; next-week forecasts are now blank.
  • The weekly activities sheet repeats three lines of report 97 word for word (manholes and catch basins, pump-station backfill, base course on road 23).
  • The RI-Register dashboard now matches its logs (3 open risks, 9 open issues), but every evidence entry still cites report 97 and the 17-11-2026 P6 update, and the schedule entries (RSK-06, ISS-10) measure slippage with cost-based progress. The cover's top five issues are unchanged from report 97.
